title: Schedules of Reinforcement & Behavior Modification
description: Analyze Fixed/Variable Ratio and Interval schedules, resistance to extinction, and token economies.

slides.title: Continuous vs. Partial Reinforcement ⏱️
slides.content:
# How Often Should You Reward?

* **Continuous Reinforcement**: Reinforcing the desired response *every single time* it occurs. Best for learning a new behavior rapidly, but extinction occurs very quickly if rewards cease.
* **Partial (Intermittent) Reinforcement**: Reinforcing a response only *part of the time*.
  * **Partial Reinforcement Extinction Effect**: Behaviors reinforced intermittently are vastly more resistant to extinction than continuously reinforced behaviors.

quizData.question: Which reinforcement schedule produces behaviors that are most stubbornly resistant to extinction?
quizData.explanation: Partial schedules create persistent behavior because the organism learns that rewards are not guaranteed on every trial.

slides.title: The Four Intermittent Schedules 🎰
slides.content:
## Ratio (Number) vs. Interval (Time)

| Schedule | Reinforcer Delivered After... | Response Pattern | Real-World Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fixed-Ratio (FR)** | A set, predictable number of responses | High rate; brief pause after reward | 'Buy 10 coffees, get 1 free' punchcard |
| **Variable-Ratio (VR)** | An unpredictable number of responses (averaged) | **Highest, steadiest response rate**; near-zero pause | Casino slot machines, lottery tickets |
| **Fixed-Interval (FI)** | First response after a set amount of time | 'Scalloped' pattern; surging responses as deadline nears | Studying intensely the night before weekly Friday quiz |
| **Variable-Interval (VI)** | First response after an unpredictable time period | Slow, steady, consistent response rate | Checking email or social media feeds |

slides.title: Applied Behavior Analysis & Token Economies 🪙
slides.content:
## Operant Principles in Real Life

**Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)** applies operant conditioning to modify socially significant human behaviors, especially in autism support, rehabilitation, and education.

### The Token Economy
An operant system where participants earn secondary reinforcers (**tokens**, chips, stars) for performing targeted positive behaviors, which can later be exchanged for backup primary reinforcers (privileges, recreation time, prizes).

quizData.question: A casino gambler repeatedly pulls the lever of a slot machine for hours because a payout could occur on any pull, averaging 1 win per 40 pulls. What schedule is this?
quizData.explanation: Variable-Ratio rewards an unpredictable number of behavioral responses, producing high and steady engagement.

slides.title: Digital Behavioral Architecture 📱
slides.content:
## The Gamification of Tech

App developers deliberately configure push notifications and infinite scrolling algorithms on **Variable-Ratio and Variable-Interval schedules**. Because users never know which swipe will reveal an exciting post or notification, the brain receives unpredictable dopamine bursts that keep users hooked.
